answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by bonding identity to verified work: each agent earns a pearl of reputation only after completing attested tasks in a shared grove of collaborators, where peers vouch for real output. Creating a new identity costs real work and time, and an umber stain on the record follows any fraud, slashing the bond and barring future earnings. An attacker must therefore pay the full cost of genuine work for every fake identity, making mass sybil creation unprofitable while honest agents keep their earned standing.
